entry.title: [PATCH net 7/7] mptcp: fix dummy mapping of overlapping segments

div.pre:
From: Geliang Tang <user28@example.test>
An MPTCP socket that has fallen back to TCP can silently lose received data if a segment partly overlaps data received earlier, and recv() then blocks, returning neither later data nor end of file.
After a fallback, subflow_check_data_avail() makes up a dummy mapping for the skb at the head of the subflow's receive queue, in which map_seq and map_subflow_seq must describe the same byte. But since commit 2834f8edd74d ("mptcp: cleanup fallback dummy mapping generation"), it computes map_seq from the first byte of the skb, while map_subflow_seq is still computed from copied_seq, the next unread byte. mptcp_subflow_get_mapped_dsn() then returns the data sequence number (DSN) of the first byte of the skb, instead of the one of copied_seq.
These two bytes differ for a segment that starts before rcv_nxt and ends after it, since TCP does not trim it. mptcp_init_skb() then gives the new bytes of this skb a DSN that is too low, and __mptcp_move_skb() skips some of them as old data, leaving a hole in the stream:
bytes 0 to 999 are received, the skb holds bytes 900 to 1499 byte 1000 gets the DSN of byte 900: too low by the 100 old bytes that is 100 below ack_seq, the next DSN that MPTCP expects __mptcp_move_skb() skips bytes 1000 to 1099 as old data ack_seq is the DSN of byte 1400, copied_seq is byte 1500 later data starts at the DSN of byte 1500: out of order the TCP FIN becomes a dummy DATA_FIN after the last byte ack_seq does not reach it, so there is no end of file
Fix this by computing map_subflow_seq from the first byte of the skb as well: mptcp_subflow_get_mapped_dsn() then returns the DSN of copied_seq.
Chris Mason sent the same fix in private, and found this issue with the help of an LLM. It has been reproduced in a VM, with the reproducer he shared, and with a new Packetdrill test: after a fallback to TCP, a segment overlapping data already received is injected. Without this patch, the new bytes at the beginning of this segment were lost, and the connection stalled, with no end of file:
reader 30.64: conn 1 BREAK: at my offset 1000 the bytes claim offset 1100: A GAP OF 100 BYTES reader 30.64: READ-TOTAL conn 1 outcome iii-gap-or-repeat bytes 1400 of 2500 [...] [...] end: hang: no data and no end of file for 30 s
And with the Packetdrill test:
dss_fallback_overlap_client.pkt:24: runtime error in read call: Expected result 2500 but got 1400 with errno 115 (Operation now in progress)

entry.title: [PATCH net 6/7] mptcp: don't send a FIN before the pending data on fallback

div.pre:
When an MPTCP connection falls back to TCP after having been shut down, the data that is still in the write queue of the MPTCP socket is lost: a FIN is sent at fallback time, and this data cannot be sent after it. This can happen with TCP Fast Open (TFO), when a server writes data and shuts the connection down before the third ACK, and this ACK has no MPTCP options.
When the MPTCP socket has been shut down, mptcp_try_fallback() also shuts the subflow down: if the DATA_FIN had already been sent, nothing would send a FIN on this subflow otherwise. The commit introducing this only considered the case where all the data had already been pushed to the subflow.
The fix used here is to only shut the subflow down at fallback time if no new data is pending, i.e. if all the data before the DATA_FIN has already been sent. Otherwise, mptcp_check_send_data_fin() will do it once this data has been pushed, e.g. by the previous commit. Pending data that has been reinjected, e.g. after the failure of another subflow, is not new: it is already in this subflow.
This issue has been found by an AI code review agent, while reviewing the code of the previous commit, and confirmed with a new Packetdrill test, where the server writes data and shuts the connection down before the third ACK, from which the MPTCP options are removed. Without this patch, a FIN was sent right after this ACK, and the data was never sent:

entry.title: [PATCH net 5/7] mptcp: push queued data on subflows falling back at the handshake

div.pre:
With TCP Fast Open, the data written by an MPTCP server before the 3rd ACK is not sent when this ACK arrives without MPTCP options, but only when another event triggers a push, e.g. new data from the peer.
The previous commit pushes this data when the third ACK, with the MP_CAPABLE option, makes a passive TFO subflow fully established. If this ACK has no MPTCP options, e.g. because a middlebox removed them, check_fully_established() falls back to TCP, and returns before this push. The fallback case of mptcp_incoming_options(), which pushes the pending data, is only reached with the next packets.
The fix used here is to push the pending data after this fallback too. Not only for the passive TFO subflows: data can also be pending on the client side, when the first ACK from the server has no MPTCP options, e.g. if the window announced by the SYN+ACK was too small for it. Same here, this data was then only sent when another event triggered a push.
This issue has been found by an AI code review agent (Clashiko), while reviewing an earlier version of the previous commit. It has been reproduced with a new Packetdrill test, where the MPTCP options are removed from the third ACK. Without this patch, and before the earlier commit "mptcp: arm the rtx timer if a push leaves data behind", this data was not sent:
server-tfo-fallback-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:26: error handling packet: Timed out waiting for packet
Since this earlier commit, this data is sent, but only when the MPTCP retransmission timer fires, here after one second, as the test increases its interval:
server-tfo-fallback-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:26: error handling packet: timing error: expected outbound packet at 0.235869 sec but happened at 1.144189 sec; tolerance 0.100000 sec
The client side case has been reported by Sashiko, while reviewing an earlier version of this commit, and confirmed with another new Packetdrill test, where the client writes more data than the window of the SYN+ACK, before an ACK without MPTCP options. Without this patch:
v1_connect_fallback_pending_data.pkt:30: error handling packet: timing error: expected outbound packet at 0.251394 sec but happened at 1.195904 sec; tolerance 0.100000 sec
Two Fixes tags: the passive TFO case comes from the first commit, and the client side one from the second one.

entry.title: [PATCH net 4/7] mptcp: push queued data on passive TFO subflows becoming established

div.pre:
With TCP Fast Open, the data written by an MPTCP server before the 3rd ACK is not sent when this ACK arrives, but only when another event triggers a push, e.g. new data from the peer. With a request/response protocol, the client waits for the reply, which can then stay stuck.
A SYN with a valid TFO cookie creates a child socket right away, which can be accepted while its subflow is still in the SYN_RECV state. The MPTCP socket is already in the ESTABLISHED state: send() puts the data in its write queue, but this data cannot be pushed to the subflow before it is established, see __mptcp_subflow_active(). When the third ACK, with the MP_CAPABLE option, arrives, check_fully_established() marks the subflow as fully established, but nothing pushes the pending data: this ACK has no DSS option, so ack_update_msk() is not called.
The fix used here is to push the pending data when a passive TFO subflow becomes fully established. Checking subflow->is_mptfo is not enough: since commit e00b63056fb4 ("mptcp: fastopen: only mark MPTFO subflows with SYN data"), it is not set when the SYN has no data, while a child is also created in this case. syn_fastopen_child is then used instead.
This issue has been reported by a user of proxies over MPTCP: the clients put their requests in the SYN, and the replies from the targets close to the server were stuck. It has been reproduced with new Packetdrill tests, where the server writes data before the third ACK, after a SYN with and without data. Without this patch, and before the earlier commit "mptcp: arm the rtx timer if a push leaves data behind", this data was not sent:
server-tfo-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:24: error handling packet: Timed out waiting for packet
Since this earlier commit, this data is sent, but only when the MPTCP retransmission timer fires, here after one second, as the tests increase its interval:
server-tfo-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:24: error handling packet: timing error: expected outbound packet at 0.237174 sec but happened at 1.181857 sec; tolerance 0.100000 sec

entry.title: [PATCH net 2/7] mptcp: push pending data after a sendmsg copy fault

div.pre:
From: Quanye Yang <user40@example.test>
mptcp_sendmsg() copies into the msk write queue first, then __mptcp_push_pending() on the success path. tcp_sendmsg_locked() does the opposite: its do_error path jumps to out, and out calls tcp_push() when copied > 0.
A later iovec fault (copy_from_iter / -EFAULT) after a successful iteration therefore returns the partial byte count but leaves the already-queued dfrag on rtx_queue. No subflow packet is sent, no retransmission timer is armed, and DATA_FIN stays blocked on first_pending.
Push in do_error when copied is already non-zero. Do not move the push to out: copied is a size_t, and sk_stream_error() stores a negative errno there.
The issue was spot by Sashiko, but easy to reproduce with Packetdrill:
writev(4, [{..., 32728}, {NULL, 4096}], 2) = 32728
Fixes: 69800e516e96 ("mptcp: propagate fastclose error") Cc: user29@example.test Closes: https://github.com/multipath-tcp/mptcp_net-next/issues/640 Signed-off-by: Quanye Yang <user40@example.test> Reviewed-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user25@example.test> Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user25@example.test> --- net/mptcp/protocol.c | 4 +++- 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
diff --git a/net/mptcp/protocol.c b/net/mptcp/protocol.c index 8968db58083e..b67096ee131b 100644 --- a/net/mptcp/protocol.c +++ b/net/mptcp/protocol.c @@ -2130,8 +2130,10 @@ static int mptcp_sendmsg(struct sock *sk, struct msghdr *msg, size_t len) return copied;
do_error: - if (copied) + if (copied) { + __mptcp_push_pending(sk, msg->msg_flags); goto out; + }
copied = sk_stream_error(sk, msg->msg_flags, ret); goto out;

entry.title: [PATCH net 1/7] mptcp: do not use a raised snd_wnd for the send window

div.pre:
ack_update_msk() sets the right edge of the MPTCP send window from the DATA_ACK and tcp_sk(ssk)->snd_wnd, but this is not always what the peer announced: mptcp_check_allowed_size() raises it to window_end - data_seq, so that TCP lets through what the MPTCP-level window allows.
That is fine for new data. For data sent again, data_seq can be below snd_una, and snd_wnd ends up too large by the difference. TCP only overwrites it when an ACK moves things forward on this subflow, see tcp_may_update_window(). If a DATA_ACK moved by another subflow comes in on this subflow before that, wnd_end goes past what the peer offered. It only moves forward, so it stays there.
The sender then transmits data beyond the peer's window: the peer drops it (MPTCP_MIB_NODSSWINDOW) after TCP acked it, and only an MPTCP-level retransmission can recover it, which raises snd_wnd again. The connection can then stay stuck at a low rate for several seconds, with nothing in flight on any subflow.
This raise has been added by commit b713d0067574 ("mptcp: really share subflow snd_wnd"), but snd_wnd could already be too large before: when nothing moves at the TCP level, tcp_may_update_window() ignores a lower non-zero window, while the peer can announce one with a DATA_ACK that moved, keeping the same right edge.
Use the window announced in the packet carrying the DATA_ACK instead.
In my case with BBR, a small TCP rmem, and a second path with a much higher latency, a lower throughput and some losses, this small change can double the throughput in the worst cases.
The issue has been reproduced with a new Packetdrill test, on a single subflow: the data is acked by TCP, then by MPTCP with a lower window, keeping the same right edge. Without this patch, the 2000 bytes written next were sent, instead of the 1280 bytes up to this right edge:
dss_dack_window_server.pkt:23: error handling packet: live packet payload: expected 1280 bytes vs actual 2000 bytes
Fixes: 6f8a612a33e4 ("mptcp: keep track of advertised windows right edge") Cc: user29@example.test Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user25@example.test> --- net/mptcp/options.c | 11 +++++++++-- 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

[PATCH net-next 2/4] eth: mpnic: add promiscuous and all-multicast filters
[PATCH net-next 1/4] eth: mpnic: add filters for dev_addr and broadcast address
[PATCH net-next 0/4] eth: mpnic: L2 address filtering

div.pre:
The mpnic device has a TCAM that is keyed on DMAC addresses in the Rx path. Up to this point, the TCAM was unprogrammed, and the default action was set to pass all traffic to the host. This series programs the TCAM to filter Rx packets based on DMAC address.
The device, broadcast, sencondary unicast and multicast addresses are added to the DMAC filter. Promiscuous and all-multicast modes are also supported by reserving the last entry in the TCAM for inexact matches.
The overall design is similar to fbnic. For each entry in the TCAM, the driver tracks the lookup key, mask, state, and users of the entry. Addresses are synced to HW in the ndo_open path, and unsynced in the ndo_stop path. ndo_set_rx_mode_async and ndo_set_mac_address are implemented, so the filtered addresses and promiscuity modes can be updated.

entry.title: [PATCH net-next] net/mlx5: E-Switch, Size FDB peer groups for asymmetric peers

div.pre:
From: Uri Dar <user96@example.test>
The slow path FDB send-to-vport and peer-miss groups are sized from the local eswitch total_vports, assuming every eswitch that may pair has the same number of vports. Per-PF VF configuration (e.g. PF_NUM_OF_VF set differently per port) breaks that assumption: the larger peer installs rules sized by its own total_vports into the smaller peer's groups, which cannot hold them, so pairing fails.
In SW and HW steering the flow table is unbounded (max_fte is INT_MAX) and flow groups are backed by dynamically grown matchers, so size the peer dependent groups to the architectural vport maximum. FW steering, whose table is bounded by log_max_ft_size, keeps the current sizing.

div.pre:
When an ARL lookup does not find the requested MAC and VID, b53_arl_read() returns the first free bin index but leaves the entry populated with the last bin examined. The multicast add path then ORs the requested port into that unrelated entry's forwarding bitmap, potentially forwarding packets to ports which are not members of the multicast group.
Clear the entry before creating a new one. Also return without writing anything when deleting an entry which is not present, instead of writing back stale bin contents. The return value for that case is unchanged (0).
